digest.component_or_area: test suite / regression verification (store read concurrency)
propositions: A fault-seeded mutation matrix (seven independent defect seeds) proves the generic reads-under-sync-contention property does NOT subsume the original CLI show regression test because seeds F3 (empty JSON output) and F6 (missing ticket_id) are caught only by the original test's content-completeness assertion
Bidirectional subsumption fails: seeds F5 (35s stall) and F7 (empty list output) are caught only by the generic property, making the two oracles complements rather than duplicates

Reverting the actual slim-fetch-ledge fix (setting _RECONVERGE_LOCK_TIMEOUT 2→15) leaves both burst tests green; only the two deterministic held-lock tests detect it, matching Go's finding that nondeterministic storm tests are unreliable oracles for specific races
Standard mutation-based test-minimization practice (Just et al. FSE 2014) licenses removal only when it does not decrease mutation score; here removal forfeits F3/F6 detection, failing the criterion
The original test's wall-clock cost (8.17–8.76s local, 12.79–14.93s Ubuntu CI) cannot be recovered by deletion without losing the partial-success detection class uniquely held by it

Both test files are retained without modification; no consolidation occurs; any future merging requires first closing the generic property's proven gap in content-completeness detection (tracked separately as stuckup-trophic-nabarlek)
